title: Deployability Signal Curator & Onboarding Staging Matrix
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Sales and Onboarding teams receive highly variable technical intake signals for Private/VPC/on-prem requests (partial proxy access, intermittent egress windows, mixed air-gapped constraints). Current triage is manual, inconsistent, and leads to misrouted engineering work, unclear SLAs, and surprise changes mid-rollout.

Proposal: Build a 'Deployability Signal Curator' that consumes intake artifacts (customer network questionnaire, connectivity probes, tenant config, security posture, requested upgrade windows) and outputs a normalized Deployability Score and an Onboarding Staging Matrix. The output will provide: a) an automated eligibility category (Green / Yellow / Red), b) prioritized remediation checklist with owner suggestions (self-serve templates for customers + internal action items), and c) a recommended rollout lane and SLA bucket for PM/SE/Delivery.

Why this matters: Normalized signals reduce manual triage time, set clear expectations with customers, and let product and engineering prioritize requests with objective economics and risk signals. This will also enable a future fast-pass automation flow for low-risk requests and a structured escalation for high-risk ones.
acceptance_criteria: Curator ingests the standard intake form and connectivity probe output and returns a Deployability Score (0-100) with rationale fields in at least 3 categories: network egress, SSH/proxy availability, and upgrade window alignment.

Output includes an Onboarding Staging Matrix that maps score ranges to recommended lanes: Green (self-serve + templated runbook), Yellow (SE-assisted staging + scheduled windows), Red (engineering review + custom workstream).

Generate templated remediation steps for the top 5 common blockers (eg. ephemeral NAT only, corporate proxy requiring allowlist, airgap with OEM package approval) with copy-paste customer instructions and internal runbook links.
PM/SE can view signal breakdown in Console mock (prototype link) and export a short summary to a customer-facing email template.

Initial curator run across 50 recent intake cases produces >=40% reduction in manual triage notes appended to tickets (measured by SE time per intake) and >=30% higher first-touch accuracy of assigned lane compared to historical baseline.
success_metrics: Mean SE triage time per intake reduced from baseline by 40% within first quarter of rollout
Percent of intakes with correct initial lane assignment >= 75% at launch
Number of support escalations caused by undisclosed network constraints reduced by 30% in 90 days
Share of requests eligible for self-serve onboarding increases by 15% over 3 months
risks: Signal quality risk: customers submit incomplete forms or inaccurate probe data leading to false Green ratings
Over-automation risk: early automation may accidentally misclassify complex bespoke networks, damaging trust
Engineering bandwidth: require ENG support for probe ingestion and Console prototype endpoints
Legal/compliance: automated recommendations must not assume privileged access; security sign-off required for templates that instruct customers to open ports.
dependencies_notes: Depends on ENG-48291 (connectivity-probe standardization) and PM-74213 (intake form consolidation). Security review required for any remediation template that instructs IP/port changes.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (2 weeks): define schema for intake signals and create canonical mapping (network-egress, proxy-type, upgrade-window, package-availability)
Phase 1 (3 weeks): build curator prototype (rule-based) and Console mock to show score + rationale; run internally against 50 historic intakes
Phase 2 (2 weeks): SE pilot with 5 customers; gather feedback, tune thresholds and remediation templates
Phase 3 (2 weeks): release read-only view to Onboarding team and enable exportable customer summary; measure metrics and iterate
Phase 4 (post-launch): evaluate ML-assisted scoring (future work) and automation for green-lane fastpass
